globalVisualTarget.summary: One continuous, physically lit private bookstore club room — not a flat product list or a stack of cards.
globalVisualTarget.room: Rich walnut cabinetry, deep bottle-green surfaces, aged-brass hardware, warm vellum/paper, controlled warm theatrical lighting, and premium letterpress/proofing-counter character throughout.
globalVisualTarget.depthPlanes: At least three visually separable depth planes are visible in every required viewport: foreground proofing counter, selected merchandise in the middle depth plane, and shelves/walls/signage behind it.
globalVisualTarget.shadows: Every object resting on a counter, shelf, stand, or turntable has a stable, coherent contact shadow; selected/neighboring/background objects cast and receive coherent shadows under one scene lighting setup; painted-on generic blob shadows fail.
globalVisualTarget.selectedItemFocus: The selected item receives the strongest local proofing light and a readable silhouette without clipping highlights or crushing material detail; it rotates continuously about its validated optical pivot on a visible turntable/plinth.
globalVisualTarget.hierarchy: Category controls, page counts, names, descriptions, balances, prices, and purchase/equip state remain legible but visually subordinate to the merchandise.
globalVisualTarget.prohibitedDrift: No military, casino, sci-fi-store, generic app-store, or arcade-shop drift; no generic mobile-store cards; no random floating panels; no oversized elements cutting into the viewport; no giant monolithic scene that crops unpredictably.

experienceFlow.summary: Opening and shopping are two camera compositions inside one continuous live 3D bookstore world (geometry, lighting, shadows, products, and selection state persist throughout). Tapping SHOP performs one uninterrupted cinematic camera move directly from the opening composition to the physical stand while opening controls fade; there is no cut, view swap, second scene/canvas, loading interstitial, or flat shop. BACK reverses the identical path.

states.description: Opening bookstore composition; camera at its deterministic opening endpoint; opening controls (including the SHOP control) fully visible and interactive.

Triggered by SHOP. One uninterrupted cinematic camera move from the opening endpoint to the deterministic shopping endpoint, inside the same scene/camera identity. Opening controls fade out during travel; no shop control becomes interactive before arrival.

Camera at its deterministic stand endpoint. The physical stand is the entire retail interface: browsing, selection, inspection, buying, and equipping all occur on it. The complete active-category assortment (13 Paper, 7 Grid, or 8 Number styles) is simultaneously visible and selectable.
Atomic physical BUY sequence on the selected product (see purchaseMechanism). Camera and scene identity are unchanged from shopping; this is a sub-state of shopping, not a new scene.
Atomic physical EQUIP sequence on the selected owned product (see equipMechanism). Camera and scene identity are unchanged from shopping; this is a sub-state of shopping, not a new scene.

Triggered by BACK. Reverses the identical camera path used by enteringShop back to the opening endpoint, inside the same scene/camera identity. Shop controls fade out during travel; opening controls fade back in only on arrival.

transitions.trigger: BUY tap on affordable unowned selected product
EQUIP tap on owned selected product

experienceFlow.inputLocking: During enteringShop and exitingShop, all interactive controls from both the opening and shop control sets are input-locked except the deterministic completion callback itself; no product, category, BUY, or EQUIP control becomes interactive until the camera has reached its deterministic endpoint and the corresponding state (shopping or opening) is entered.
experienceFlow.completionCallbacks: enteringShop and exitingShop each resolve through exactly one deterministic completion callback fired when the camera reaches its locked endpoint transform; the callback both unlocks the destination state's controls and commits the state-machine transition atomically (no window where controls are interactive but the state machine has not yet transitioned, and no window where the state has transitioned but controls remain locked).
experienceFlow.repeatedTapHandling: Repeated SHOP taps while already in enteringShop or shopping are ignored (coalesced to a no-op); repeated BACK taps while already in exitingShop or opening are ignored. Taps are never queued to restart, reverse mid-flight, or double-travel the camera path.
experienceFlow.interruptionAndBackgroundRecovery: If the app is backgrounded or interrupted during enteringShop or exitingShop, on foreground return the camera deterministically resumes the in-progress path to its locked destination endpoint — under standard motion by continuing the same eased interpolation, or under Reduce Motion by a zero-duration transform interpolation to that same endpoint executed by the same live camera inside the same live 3D scene; it never resumes from a stranded intermediate pose and never silently reverts to the opposite endpoint.
experienceFlow.cancellationPolicy: enteringShop and exitingShop are not user-cancellable mid-flight; once triggered they run to their deterministic destination endpoint. BACK issued during purchasing or equipping does not start exitingShop until the atomic purchase/equip sequence reaches a deterministic completion or a defined safe-cancellation point (see purchaseMechanism/equipMechanism); it is queued, not dropped.
experienceFlow.raceConditionPrevention: The state machine exposes exactly one authoritative current state and one authoritative in-flight transition at a time; SHOP, BACK, BUY, and EQUIP triggers are serialized against that single in-flight transition so the camera can never be asked to travel two directions at once or strand between opening and shopping endpoints.
experienceFlow.deterministicCameraEndpoints: opening and shopping each resolve to one fixed, versioned camera transform (position, orientation, FOV) per device/orientation/safe-area configuration; enteringShop always interpolates opening-endpoint to shopping-endpoint and exitingShop always interpolates the same path in reverse, never a different or approximate endpoint.
experienceFlow.reduceMotionBehavior: Reduce Motion may shorten the enteringShop/exitingShop travel duration, or replace the eased interpolation with a zero-duration transform interpolation directly to the same two deterministic endpoints, executed by the same live camera inside the same live 3D scene used by standard motion. Either form must still transition between the exact opening and shopping camera transforms; preserve geometry, lighting, shadow, product, and selection-state continuity throughout; execute the identical enteringShop/exitingShop state-machine states, transitions, and completion callbacks defined above; and preserve the identical opening/shop control cross-fade behavior. It may never replace the single scene/camera with a second scene, canvas, or view, never flatten the shop into a non-3D view, and never instantiate or reveal a second renderer/view/scene at any point. This is the only meaning of any zero-duration or instantaneous camera transform in this document; any other use of the words cut or snap below refers exclusively to prohibited behavior.
experienceFlow.sameSceneRequirement: opening and shopping (and all sub-states) render through exactly one 3D scene/camera/root node; no separate SwiftUI screen, second RealityKit/SceneKit scene, or navigation push/replace may present shopping content. The flat ClubShopView is never reachable from this state machine in a release build.
prohibited: Any camera cut, hard snap that bypasses the live camera/scene, view swap, second scene/canvas, or loading interstitial between opening and shopping, including under Reduce Motion.
A flat shop screen, generic card list, popup storefront, sheet, or separate confirmation screen presented in place of, or on top of, the physical stand.
A camera left stranded at a non-deterministic intermediate pose after interruption, repeated taps, or race conditions.

Reduce Motion implemented as a swap, cut, or snap to a different, non-continuous view/scene/renderer instead of the same live camera's zero-duration transform interpolation inside the same live 3D scene.

physicalStandRetail.summary: The physical stand is the entire store. Browsing, selection, inspection, buying, and equipping all occur through the physical stand; flat ClubShopView, generic card lists, popups, sheets, and separate confirmation screens are explicitly release-rejected.

responsiveFraming.description: Responsive framing may use multiple physical tiers/depth rows while keeping every active-category product visible simultaneously; it may not virtualize, paginate, clip, drawer, end-mark, or selected-plus-neighbor-shortcut any product away.

measurableBounds.silhouetteSeparation: Every pair of adjacent resting-pose products maintains at least 4pt (compact) / 6pt (standard and larger) of unoccluded silhouette gap on every shared edge, verified by automated bounding-box and alpha-mask overlap checks per device.
measurableBounds.legibility: Every resting active-category product has a projected on-screen silhouette whose shorter screen-space dimension is at least 24pt on compact devices and at least 32pt on standard/larger devices, measured in its resting pose at native device resolution (this replaces and invalidates the prior '3% of the shorter viewport dimension' floor, which could produce an approximately 11-point object on compact hardware and did not prove the user could choose it). Thin paper/grid forms, whose resting silhouette is a flat sheet, may satisfy this floor using their longer on-screen dimension together with the required physicalNameTag below, provided neither the product nor its tag is ever hidden. Every product is individually distinguishable (category, style) in the required per-category contact-sheet screenshot at native device resolution, and human screenshot review must correctly identify all 13 Paper, all 7 Grid, and all 8 Number products from their fully populated category frame. This floor may only increase from later real-device evidence that proves it insufficient; it may never be lowered merely to fit 13/7/8 — responsive tiers, camera composition, and stand geometry must solve fit while every active-category product stays simultaneously visible.
measurableBounds.physicalNameTag: Every product has its own non-overlapping physical name/style tag (vellum or brass placard) that is legible at native device resolution without zoom or selection, in addition to and never obscuring the product silhouette itself. The tag's default text is at least 11 points before Dynamic Type scaling, and meets the existing contrast/accessibility requirements in VISUAL_INVARIANTS.md. The tag never substitutes for the product silhouette; both must be simultaneously visible.
measurableBounds.hitTargets: Every selectable product retains its own independent hit target of at least 44x44 points, separate from any neighboring product's hit target, regardless of tier/row, per VISUAL_INVARIANTS.md #5.
measurableBounds.occlusion: No resting-pose active-category product may be more than 15% occluded (by bounding-box/alpha-mask area) by another product, control, or fixture; the product on the central proofing platform is unoccluded.
measurableBounds.zFighting: No two coplanar or near-coplanar thin assets (paper/grid) may render with visible z-fighting; a minimum authored world-space separation is enforced between adjacent thin assets sharing a tier/row.
measurableBounds.shadows: Every visible product at every tier/row has its own coherent contact shadow consistent with scene lighting; a single shared painted-on blob shadow never substitutes for per-product/per-tier shadowing.

physicalStandRetail.numberStyleDigitDemonstration: A selected Number style simultaneously demonstrates digits 1-9 together at inspection scale on the stand/proofing platform; the player selects and purchases/equips the style package as one product, not nine independent catalog products.
physicalStandRetail.selectionMechanism: Selecting a product physically moves or hands it into the central lit, shadowed, rotating proofing platform (see shop-display-proofing-bay-turntable / shop-environment-proofing-stand families) while every other active-category product remains simultaneously visible at its deterministic stand position; no other product disappears, virtualizes, or relocates off-stand during selection.
physicalStandRetail.browseableStatesPreserved: Locked, affordable, insufficient-balance, owned, and equipped states remain browseable and physically visible; state may alter controls/copy but may never hide the physical item.
prohibited: Flat ClubShopView, generic card list, popup storefront, sheet, or separate confirmation screen used for browsing, buying, or equipping.
Any technique in prohibitedHidingTechniques used to reduce the simultaneously-visible count below 13/7/8.
A fourth Desk category or any reduction of the 13/7/8/72 catalog truth.

purchaseMechanism.summary: On a successful affordable BUY, the authoritative balance/ownership transaction is validated, submitted, and its persistence confirmed first; only then does the physical brass stamp press onto the selected product's vellum price tag, and stamp contact reveals the already-persisted OWNED tag and decremented balance while firing the impact sound/haptic. The stamp never contacts, and no success feedback is ever shown, before persistence is confirmed.

sequence.description: BUY control tap on the selected, affordable, unowned product; control is gated (disabled/no-op) for insufficient balance, already-owned, or while a purchase/equip sequence is already in flight. The brass stamp remains at rest.

Balance and ownership are re-validated against the single authoritative state owner before any physical/visual change begins; insufficient balance, already-owned, or any other validation failure aborts here — the stamp never moves, and no decrement, OWNED tag, sound, or haptic occurs.

On successful validation, one atomic authoritative transaction (balance decrement + ownership write) is submitted for persistence. The brass stamp remains at rest during submission; a non-confirming pending/accessibility state (e.g. a busy indicator or VoiceOver 'processing purchase' announcement) may be shown, but it must not imitate stamp contact, play the impact sound, fire the impact haptic, show a decremented balance, or show OWNED.

The single atomic commit point: this phase is entered only when the submitted transaction's persistence is confirmed by the authoritative state owner. If persistence fails here, the sequence moves directly to the persistenceFailure outcome in failureAndRollback and the stamp never presses.
Only after confirmedPersistence: the physical brass stamp begins its press motion toward the vellum price tag.
The stamp reaches full downward travel.

The stamp face contacts the vellum tag. Because persistence was already confirmed in the confirmedPersistence phase, contact is the frame that reveals the already-persisted balance decrement and OWNED tag and fires the stamp-impact sound and haptic hooks, synchronized to this frame. Contact never occurs, and these effects never fire, unless confirmedPersistence was already reached.
The stamp lifts away from the tag; the revealed OWNED tag and decremented balance remain displayed.

A VoiceOver purchase-confirmation announcement fires naming the product and the new balance; this is a presentation step only and does not gate or re-trigger the already-confirmed persisted state shown at contact.

purchaseMechanism.soundAndHapticHooks: A stamp-impact sound effect and a haptic impact feed fire exactly once, synchronized to the contact phase, and only ever after confirmedPersistence has already been reached for that transaction; they never fire during input/authoritativeValidation/submitTransaction/press/down/release, and never fire without a corresponding authoritative transaction having already confirmed persistence.
purchaseMechanism.inputGating: The BUY control and every other purchase/equip control on the stand are input-locked for the full input-through-confirmation sequence; duplicate/repeated taps during that window are ignored (coalesced to a no-op), never queued to double-submit, double-press, or double-decrement.
purchaseMechanism.transactionalOrdering: Balance decrement and ownership-flag write are one atomic authoritative transaction whose persistence is confirmed strictly before the physical stamp press begins. The physical press, down, and contact phases, the stamp-impact sound/haptic, the displayed balance decrement, and the OWNED tag every one of them individually and all of them together never precede confirmed persistence of that transaction; and the stamp is never at rest showing OWNED/decremented state without a corresponding confirmed persisted transaction.
purchaseMechanism.accessibilityAnnouncement: VoiceOver announces purchase start (product name, price, current balance) on input, an optional non-committing 'processing purchase' state during submitTransaction, and purchase result (success with the new balance and OWNED state, announced no earlier than confirmedPersistence, or the specific failure reason) on completion; the physical OWNED tag has a localized accessible state matching the visual state.
purchaseMechanism.reduceMotionEquivalent: Under Reduce Motion, submitTransaction/confirmedPersistence are unchanged (persistence is still confirmed before any physical stamp motion), and the press/down/contact/release motion is shortened or replaced by a zero-duration transform interpolation to the same post-persistence stamp-contact pose, executed by the same live camera/scene; the physical stamp/tag state change, sound, and haptic confirmation are preserved at that same post-persistence commit point, never removed and never moved earlier than confirmedPersistence.

failureAndRollback.insufficientBalance: BUY is a no-op at authoritativeValidation, before submitTransaction and before any stamp animation starts; the stamp remains at rest; no decrement, no OWNED tag, no sound, no haptic; a truthful insufficient-balance message is shown and announced; state remains exactly unchanged.
failureAndRollback.duplicateOrAlreadyOwnedInput: Ignored (no-op) at authoritativeValidation while a purchase is in flight for that product or any other product on the stand, or when the product is already owned; never produces a second stamp, second decrement, or a queued double-purchase; the stamp remains at rest and state remains exactly unchanged.
failureAndRollback.cancellationBeforeSubmission: The sequence may be safely cancelled up through the end of authoritativeValidation (before submitTransaction begins) with no transaction submitted, no stamp motion, and no state change. Once submitTransaction has begun, the sequence is not user-cancellable and always runs to a deterministic confirmedPersistence-then-contact outcome or an authoritative persistenceFailure outcome.
failureAndRollback.backgrounding: If the app is backgrounded during submitTransaction or confirmedPersistence, on foreground return the sequence resumes based strictly on the authoritative persisted transaction state: if persistence had already confirmed, the physical stamp press/down/contact/release/confirmation completes deterministically (revealing the already-true OWNED/decremented state); if persistence had not confirmed or failed, the sequence rolls back to the pre-purchase state with the stamp at rest and no decrement/OWNED tag shown. It never resumes into a visually ambiguous half-stamped state, and the product is never charged without eventually showing truthful ownership/balance state.
failureAndRollback.persistenceFailure: If the submitted transaction fails to persist (at confirmedPersistence), the balance is not decremented, the tag never changes to OWNED, the brass stamp never presses and remains at rest, no impact sound or haptic fires, and a truthful failure message is shown and announced; the pre-purchase physical and balance state is restored/left exactly unchanged. State remains exactly unchanged.

purchaseMechanism.postconditionInvariant: It is never possible to observe stamp contact, the stamp-impact sound/haptic, a decremented balance, or an OWNED tag without a corresponding already-confirmed persisted purchase transaction; and it is never possible for a transaction to confirm persistence while leaving the eventual truthful physical OWNED/decremented state permanently unshown (interruption before contact completes deterministically on foreground/re-entry per the backgrounding rule above).

equipMechanism.summary: On EQUIP, the owned product mechanically slides or rotates into the central proofing position, the proofing lamp brightens, and the physical brass plaque changes to EQUIPPED only after equip state persists.

sequence.description: EQUIP control tap on the selected, owned, not-currently-equipped product; control is gated (disabled/no-op) for unowned products or while a purchase/equip sequence is already in flight.
Ownership and current-equipped state are re-validated against the single authoritative state owner immediately before any physical/visual change begins.

The owned product mechanically slides or rotates from its stand position into the central proofing position; the previously equipped product (if any) simultaneously or immediately thereafter mechanically returns to its deterministic stand position.
The proofing lamp brightens to its equipped-focus intensity, synchronized with the mechanical move.
The authoritative equip-state transaction (new equipped id, previous equipped id cleared) is submitted for persistence, synchronized with the mechanical move completing.
Only after the equip state persists does the physical brass plaque change to EQUIPPED and a VoiceOver equip-confirmation announcement fires naming the newly equipped product.

equipMechanism.priorItemReturn: The previously equipped product returns to its deterministic stand position as part of the same atomic sequence; it is never left in the central proofing position, off-stand, or in a visually ambiguous intermediate pose after the sequence completes.
equipMechanism.inputGating: The EQUIP control and every other purchase/equip control on the stand are input-locked for the full mechanicalMove-through-confirmation sequence; duplicate/repeated taps are ignored (coalesced to a no-op).
equipMechanism.selectionAndEquippedStateTruthfulness: Selection state (which product is on the proofing platform for inspection) and equipped state (which product is the plaque-confirmed EQUIPPED product) remain independently truthful during repeated/racing actions, interruption, relaunch, VoiceOver navigation, and Reduce Motion; selecting a product for inspection never implicitly changes the equipped product, and equipping never silently changes the browsing selection of a different category.
equipMechanism.accessibility: VoiceOver announces equip start (product name, current equipped product) on input, and equip result (success with new EQUIPPED product, or the specific failure reason) on completion; the physical EQUIPPED plaque has a localized accessible state matching the visual state.
equipMechanism.reduceMotionEquivalent: Under Reduce Motion the slide/rotate mechanical move and lamp brighten are shortened or replaced by a direct state change at the same commit point; the physical mechanical position change, lamp state, and EQUIPPED plaque change are preserved, never removed.

failureAndRollback.duplicateOrRepeatedInput: Ignored while an equip sequence is in flight; never produces two simultaneous mechanical moves or a queued double-equip.
failureAndRollback.interruptionOrBackgrounding: If backgrounded mid-sequence, on foreground return the sequence resumes to its deterministic outcome based on the authoritative persisted equip state; it never resumes into a state where two products appear equipped or the plaque contradicts the persisted state.
failureAndRollback.persistenceFailure: If the authoritative equip-state transaction fails to persist, the mechanical move visually reverses (or never completes), the plaque never changes to EQUIPPED, and a truthful failure message is announced; the pre-equip physical and equipped state is restored exactly.

equipMechanism.postconditionInvariant: It is never possible to observe an EQUIPPED plaque without a corresponding successfully persisted equip transaction naming that product, and never possible to observe a persisted equip transaction without the plaque and central-position state matching it.

reversePathAndPersistence.summary: BACK from shopping reverses the same camera path to the opening composition; shop controls fade out and opening controls return. No cut, reload, or new scene is permitted.
reversePathAndPersistence.cameraReversal: exitingShop always interpolates the identical spatial path used by enteringShop, in reverse, to the same deterministic opening endpoint; it is not a different or approximate path.
reversePathAndPersistence.controlCrossfade: Shop controls fade out during exitingShop travel; opening controls fade back in only on arrival at the opening endpoint (the same completion-callback-gated timing as enteringShop's fade-out of opening controls).
reversePathAndPersistence.persistenceScope: Selected category and selected product persist through exit (BACK), the restored opening state, re-entry (next SHOP), app backgrounding, and relaunch, wherever the product contract requires persistence (ownership and equip state always; category/product selection at minimum across exit/re-entry and relaunch).
reversePathAndPersistence.authoritativeStateOwner: Exactly one authoritative state owner (a single source-of-truth store/service) holds selectedCategory, selectedProductId, ownership, and equip state; the shop scene, opening scene, and any persistence layer all read from and write through that one owner rather than maintaining independent copies that can drift.

inFlightTransactionAtExit.rule: If a purchase or equip transaction is in its atomic physical sequence (purchasing or equipping state) when BACK is invoked, exitingShop is deferred until that sequence reaches a deterministic completion or a defined safe-cancellation point.
prohibited: Charging (decrementing balance / marking OWNED) without the transaction's ownership state being persisted.
Showing OWNED or EQUIPPED visual/accessible state without the corresponding state having actually persisted.
Exiting mid-sequence in a way that strands the physical stamp, mechanical move, or lamp state in an intermediate pose.

reversePathAndPersistence.reEntryReachability: On the next SHOP, enteringShop's destination shopping state restores the persisted selectedCategory and selectedProductId exactly, with the previously purchased/equipped physical states reflected truthfully on the stand.

deviceOrientationStateMatrix.rule: Every requiredFrames entry is captured for every device/orientation/state combination in this matrix, not only a single representative device.

automatedAssertions: State-transition graph matches experienceFlow.states/transitions exactly (opening, enteringShop, shopping, purchasing, equipping, exitingShop, back to opening).
Single camera/scene identity: shopping content never renders through a second scene, canvas, or navigation push/replace; flat ClubShopView is not release-reachable from any entry point.
Input/race behavior: repeated SHOP/BACK/BUY/EQUIP taps, interruption, and backgrounding never strand the camera or produce a double transaction.
Simultaneous product visibility: exactly 13 Paper, 7 Grid, or 8 Number style products are visible and selectable at once in the active category, for every device/orientation in the matrix.

Deterministic selection: selecting a product always yields the same canonical registry id, moves it to the same central proofing position, and leaves every other active-category product at its deterministic stand position.

Exact-once purchase: a successful BUY decrements the stamp balance exactly once and sets OWNED exactly once per product; no double-charge or false stamp is reachable via any input sequence in this contract.
Equip persistence: EQUIPPED state and the returned prior item's position survive relaunch and match the authoritative state owner.
Reverse camera endpoints: exitingShop always terminates at the same deterministic opening endpoint used by the initial opening state.
Flat ClubShopView is not release-reachable: a reachability test enumerates every navigation path and asserts ClubShopView is never presented in a release configuration.
negativeAssertions: No responsive rule permits an end marker, compact-screen exception, paging, or a selected-plus-neighbors shortcut to stand in for any active-category product; the prior responsiveRules.clipping allowance for a compact-screen end marker is corrected and removed by this document.
No carousel virtualization, clipping, overflow drawer, or pagination control reduces the simultaneously-visible count below 13/7/8.
No popup, sheet, or separate confirmation screen replaces the physical stamp/tag BUY confirmation or the physical plaque EQUIP confirmation.
performanceEvidence: Both camera directions (enteringShop and exitingShop) profiled for frame time and memory against the existing PERFORMANCE_BUDGETS.md without relaxing budgets.
Fully populated stands (13/7/8 simultaneously visible) profiled at worst-case device (DEV-COMPACT) and at DEV-PHYSICAL.
Selected-item rotation profiled during and independent of camera travel.
BUY and EQUIP sequences profiled end-to-end including sound/haptic hook timing.

responsiveRules.orientation: Portrait and every supported orientation must be captured per device; no captured orientation may clip a horizontal edge.
responsiveRules.safeArea: Camera framing is safe-area/Dynamic-Island/home-indicator aware; controls and labels must not overlap the product silhouette, turntable, safe area, or each other.
responsiveRules.tapTargets: Every interactive control has a hit target of at least 44 by 44 points, locked from VISUAL_INVARIANTS.md #5.
clipping: Zero clipping or intersection: merchandise, controls, and neighbors must not clip either horizontal edge or intersect the counter or each other.

Complete first/middle/last reachability: for every category, the first, middle, penultimate, and last catalog item must be selectable through visible controls, swipe/drag, keyboard arrows where available, and VoiceOver.
Truthful denominators: Paper shows X / 13, Grid shows X / 7, Numbers shows X / 8, always matching the true catalog count.
Selected-item containment: the selected item never drifts outside its display bay.

Neighbor behavior: previous/next items, and every other active-category product regardless of device size, stay fully visible, individually selectable, inside counter/stand boundaries, and visually subordinate to the selected item; no end marker (including any compact-screen exception), virtualization, pagination, clipping, overflow drawer, or selected-plus-neighbors shortcut may stand in for any active-category product on any device, per physicalStandRetail.
Optical-pivot drift tolerance: 2 points on the compact phone or 0.5% of viewport width on any larger phone, whichever is stricter, across one full revolution.
responsiveRules.dynamicType: Runtime text (names, prices, descriptions, balances, state copy) supports Dynamic Type without breaking the 44pt tap targets or causing overlap with merchandise.
responsiveRules.voiceOver: Focus order follows category → merchandise navigation → selected product details → price/state → purchase/equip. Every physical product has a localized accessible name and state; loading/error states are announced.
responsiveRules.reduceMotion: Automatic turntable spin and effect animation (flame/laser pulse, laser-grid travel) stop or simplify; a direct drag or accessible "Rotate preview" action remains available; purchase/selection/inspection remain fully available.

effectLeaves.note: The two physical flame components for nb_flame (crown, embers).

families.positiveFormDirection: Each of the nine digits is a complete, independently modeled numeral whose primary subject is exactly one recognizable digit; the digit itself is the merchandise. All nine digits share cap height, depth, bevel language, material language, lighting response, and front axis. Catalog identity: "Press" — The face the Book is set in.
families.materialDirection: Letterpress-cast metal type: crisp incised serif digits with a slight ink-squeeze bevel, dark oxidised lead-alloy body, subtle proofing-oil sheen.
families.detailDirection: Width may vary naturally by numeral, but optical scale stays consistent across 1–9. The complete numeral silhouette remains intact at every required scale; decorative or effect elements stay outside or behind the readable core.
exclusions: No ball, sphere, typewriter body, keycap, pedestal, plaque, or surrounding machine as part of the digit merchandise unless the approved style explicitly requires a direct attached element that does not impair gameplay.

rejectionRules: Theme drift away from private-bookstore walnut/bottle-green/aged-brass/vellum character into generic mobile-store cards, casino, military, arcade, or sci-fi-store presentation.
Flat/generic card-store output in place of a continuous, physically lit 3D room with at least three visible depth planes.
A monolithic, precomposed room model that crops unpredictably instead of a modular, aspect-ratio-aware kit.
Any missing product, missing digit (1–9), or missing grid/paper package against the 13/7/8 catalog truth.
A shop preview that uses unrelated art from the gameplay asset, or vice versa (fake shop/gameplay asset mismatch).
Any digit whose readability depends on bloom/emissive being enabled.
Generic toilet paper: a tinted/generic white plane standing in for the Utility Roll shop or gameplay deliverable.
Floating or intersecting objects: any merchandise, control, or fixture without a coherent contact shadow, or that intersects the counter, neighboring products, or controls.
Painted-on generic blob shadows in place of coherent scene-consistent contact/cast shadows.
Pivot drift beyond the locked tolerance (2pt compact / 0.5% viewport width larger, whichever stricter) during a full turntable revolution.
Use of any reference not listed in approvedReferenceIds for this package, including MOCKUP-SHOP-001/002 or SCREENSHOT-CLUBSHOP-001, to govern generation.
Any procedural primitive, SwiftUI Shape/Path/Canvas/gradient, SF Symbol, or font glyph substituting for required Meshy-origin art.
Incomplete provenance: missing Meshy task id, missing prompt/checksum, missing preserved source, or missing registry mapping for any canonical id in this package.
Any flat ClubShopView, generic card list, popup, sheet, or separate confirmation screen release-reachable for browsing, buying, or equipping in place of the physical stand (see physicalStandRetail).

Any responsive rule permitting an end marker, compact-screen exception, paging, virtualization, overflow drawer, or selected-plus-neighbors shortcut to hide any active-category product below the required 13/7/8 simultaneous count (see physicalStandRetail.prohibitedHidingTechniques).

A camera cut, second scene/canvas, loading interstitial, or view swap between the opening composition and the physical stand in either travel direction, including any Reduce Motion implementation that cuts, hard-snaps outside the live camera/scene, or swaps to a second renderer/view/scene instead of a same-scene zero-duration transform interpolation (see experienceFlow.reduceMotionBehavior).

A false BUY stamp, double stamp-balance decrement, premature OWNED/EQUIPPED state, or lost selection/ownership/equip persistence across exit, re-entry, backgrounding, or relaunch (see purchaseMechanism, equipMechanism, reversePathAndPersistence).

Any stamp press, down, contact, impact sound, impact haptic, displayed balance decrement, or OWNED tag shown before the authoritative balance/ownership transaction has confirmed persistence, for any reason including insufficient funds, duplicate/already-owned input, cancellation before submission, or persistence failure (see purchaseMechanism.sequence and purchaseMechanism.failureAndRollback).

A browseability floor for any active-category product lower than 24pt (compact) / 32pt (standard/larger) shorter screen-space silhouette dimension, or a missing independent 44x44pt hit target, or a missing/overlapping/sub-11pt physical name/style tag, used to make 13/7/8 fit on any device (see physicalStandRetail.responsiveFraming.measurableBounds.legibility and .physicalNameTag).

phaseOwnershipNotes.meshyModelSelection: The exact Meshy model/mode/pricing selection is owned by Phase 3 (sonnet-meshy-pipeline-engineer) after live inspection of current official Meshy API documentation and changelog at execution time. This Phase 2 package does not pin any Meshy model identifier, mode default, or price.
phaseOwnershipNotes.generationReferenceSheets: Any orthographic/clean generation-reference sheet produced for a family in Phase 3 is a production input only. It may never ship as runtime art, a shop/gameplay thumbnail, or a fallback asset.
phaseOwnershipNotes.experienceFlowScope: experienceFlow, physicalStandRetail, purchaseMechanism, equipMechanism, reversePathAndPersistence, and flowEvidenceGates are non-redesignable interaction/architecture requirements layered onto the existing 208-row asset ledger; they add zero new canonical asset ids and do not change totalLedgerIds, visibleProductionIds, deadCodeDispositionIds, or familyCount. They are owned jointly by Phase 8 (shop scene/environment), Phase 9 (registry/purchase/equip/persistence integration), and Phase 10 (motion/presentation) rather than by a new asset family.
